tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

## Introduction MMDetection3D is an open source object detection toolbox based on PyTorch, towards the next-generation platform for general 3D detection. It is a part of the [OpenMMLab](https://openmmlab.com/) project. The main branch works with **PyTorch 1.8+**. ![demo image](resources/mmdet3d_outdoor_demo.gif)
Major features - **Support multi-modality/single-modality detectors out of box** It directly supports multi-modality/single-modality detectors including MVXNet, VoteNet, PointPillars, etc. - **Support indoor/outdoor 3D detection out of box** It directly supports popular indoor and outdoor 3D detection datasets, including ScanNet, SUNRGB-D, Waymo, nuScenes, Lyft, and KITTI. For nuScenes dataset, we also support [nuImages dataset](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/tree/main/configs/nuimages). - **Natural integration with 2D detection** All the about **300+ models, methods of 40+ papers**, and modules supported in [MMDetection](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection/blob/3.x/docs/en/model_zoo.md) can be trained or used in this codebase. - **High efficiency** It trains faster than other codebases. The main results are as below. Details can be found in [benchmark.md](./docs/en/notes/benchmarks.md). We compare the number of samples trained per second (the higher, the better). # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你不能：

- 修改源码
- 写入任何 `.md` 文件
- 输出 JSON 以外的文字

你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。

---

## 总目标

为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。

这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。

每篇讲义应该满足：

1. 面向初学者也能读懂。
2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。
3. 必须结合真实源码。
4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。

---

## 源码探查顺序

请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节：

1. 项目说明
   - README
   - docs
   - examples
   - tutorials

2. 构建与运行方式
   - package.json
   - Cargo.toml
   - pyproject.toml
   - go.mod
   - pom.xml
   - Makefile
   - Dockerfile
   - CI 配置

3. 项目入口
   - CLI 入口
   - Web 服务入口
   - main 文件
   - library export 文件
   - examples 入口

4. 目录结构
   - src
   - lib
   - app
   - packages
   - crates
   - tests

5. 核心流程
   - 初始化流程
   - 配置加载
   - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路
   - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制

6. 测试与示例
   - 单元测试
   - 集成测试
   - benchmark
   - example usage

---

## 学习路线设计原则

请把学习手册设计成三层：

1. 入门层 beginner
   目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。

2. 进阶层 intermediate
   目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。

3. 专家层 advanced
   目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。

---

## 讲义拆分规则

- 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。
- 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。
- 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。
- 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。
- 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。
- 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。
- 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。
- 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。

---

## mode=full

首次生成大纲时：

1. 阅读项目关键文件。
2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。
3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。
4. 输出完整 manifest。
5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。

---

## mode=incremental

增量更新时：

1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。
2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。
3. 使用：

   - `git diff previous_head..current_head`
   - `git log`
   - `git show`

   分析代码变化。

4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。

每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置：

- `"keep"`
  代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。

- `"update"`
  小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。

- `"new"`
  新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。

- `"rebuild"`
  架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。

如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。

---

## manifest 输出格式

只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。

```json

  "project": "<项目名>",
  "head": "<current_head>",
  "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。",
  "units": [
    {
      "id": "u1",
      "title": "单元标题",
      "level": "beginner",
      "order": 1,
      "lectures": [
        {
          "id": "u1-l1",
          "title": "讲义标题",
          "order": 1,
          "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md",
          "level": "beginner",
          "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。",
          "learning_goals": [
            "学习目标 1",
            "学习目标 2"
          ],
          "source_files": [
            "README.md",
            "src/main.ts"
          ],
          "minimal_modules": [
            "模块 1",
            "模块 2"
          ],
          "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。",
          "depends_on": [],
          "action": "new"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

## 字段要求

- `project`：项目名。
- `head`：当前 git HEAD。
- `rationale`：中文，一段即可。
- `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。
- `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。
- `filename`：
  - 必须全局唯一。
  - 必须小写。
  - 使用连字符。
  - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。
  - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。
- `level`：
  - `"beginner"`
  - `"intermediate"`
  - `"advanced"`
- `source_files`：
  - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。
  - 不要编造文件路径。
- `depends_on`：
  - 使用讲义 id。
  - 没有依赖时填写空数组。
- `action`：
  - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。
  - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。

---

## 重要约束

- 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。
- 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。
- 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。
- 输出必须是合法 JSON。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),

        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

63 64 ## Introduction 65 66 MMDetection3D is an open source object detection toolbox based on PyTorch, towards the next-generation platform for general 3D detection. It is a part of the [OpenMMLab](https://openmmlab.com/) project. 67 68 The main branch works with **PyTorch 1.8+**. 69 70 ![demo image](resources/mmdet3d_outdoor_demo.gif) 71 72
73 Major features 74 75 - **Support multi-modality/single-modality detectors out of box** 76 77 It directly supports multi-modality/single-modality detectors including MVXNet, VoteNet, PointPillars, etc. 78 79 - **Support indoor/outdoor 3D detection out of box** 80 81 It directly supports popular indoor and outdoor 3D detection datasets, including ScanNet, SUNRGB-D, Waymo, nuScenes, Lyft, and KITTI. For nuScenes dataset, we also support [nuImages dataset](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/tree/main/configs/nuimages). 82 83 - **Natural integration with 2D detection** 84 85 All the about **300+ models, methods of 40+ papers**, and modules supported in [MMDetection](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection/blob/3.x/docs/en/model_zoo.md) can be trained or used in this codebase. 86 87 - **High efficiency** 88 89 It trains faster than other codebases. # Copyright (c) OpenMMLab. All rights reserved.
import argparse
import logging
import os
import os.path as osp

from mmengine.config import Config, DictAction
from mmengine.logging import print_log
from mmengine.registry import RUNNERS
from mmengine.runner import Runner

from mmdet3d.utils import replace_ceph_backend


def parse_args():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Train a 3D detector')
    parser.add_argument('config', help='train config file path')
    parser.add_argument('--work-dir', help='the dir to save logs and models')
    parser.add_argument(
        '--amp',
        action='store_true',
        default=False,
        help='enable automatic-mixed-precision training')
    parser.add_argument(
        '--sync_bn',
        choices=['none', 'torch', 'mmcv'],
        default='none',
        help='convert all BatchNorm layers in the model to SyncBatchNorm '
        '(SyncBN) or mmcv.ops.sync_bn.SyncBatchNorm (MMSyncBN) layers.')
    parser.add_argument(
        '--auto-scale-lr',
        action='store_true',
        help='enable automatically scaling LR.')
    parser.add_argument(
        '--resume',
        nargs='?',
        type=str,
        const='auto',
        help='If specify checkpoint path, resume from it, while if not '
        'specify, try to auto resume from the latest checkpoint '

units.title: 3D 分割、扩展开发与项目生态

input.head: fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b
input.rationale: MMDetection3D 是基于 MMEngine 配置驱动架构的大型 3D 检测工具箱，代码量大、模块多，因此按「先会用、再懂结构、后懂算法、终能扩展」的顺序分 8 个单元 43 篇讲义。单元 1 让读者从零安装并跑通 demo，理解配置系统这一贯穿全库的骨架；单元 2 集中讲解坐标系与 BaseInstance3DBoxes/BasePoints/Det3DDataSample 这组全库通用的数据契约，这是 3D 领域最独特也最容易踩坑的部分，必须先于数据管线和模型讲解；单元 3 沿「原始数据 → info pkl → 数据集类 → 加载/增强/采样/打包管线」的真实数据流推进；单元 4 讲注册器机制与检测器基类，作为进入模型世界的门；单元 5、6 分别沿自动驾驶主线（体素/柱体 → SECOND → Anchor/CenterPoint → 任务模块与损失）和点云/单目/多模态主线（PointNet++ → VoteNet → 两阶段 → MVXNet）拆解模型算法，体素线在前因为它概念更少、链路最完整；单元 7 覆盖训练测试全流程、评估指标、可视化、推理器与实用工具；单元 8 面向二次开发，讲 3D 分割、自定义数据集与模型、projects 生态与测试贡献流程。依赖关系严格按数据结构 → 管线 → 模型 → 训练评估 → 扩展排列，确保每篇讲义只依赖已讲内容。

learning_goals: 说出 MMDetection3D 支持的任务类型（LiDAR 检测、视觉 3D 检测、多模态、3D 分割）与支持的数据集
理解它与 MMEngine、MMCV、MMDetection 的依赖与复用关系
了解 configs、projects、tools、mmdet3d 四大目录的分工
lectures.title: 项目全景：MMDetection3D 是什么
lectures.topic: 介绍 MMDetection3D 的定位：基于 PyTorch 的通用 3D 检测工具箱，支持点云、图像、多模态三大输入，以及它在 OpenMMLab 生态中与 MMEngine/MMCV/MMDetection 的关系。

learning_goals: 正确安装 mmengine、mmcv、mmdet 与 mmdet3d 并理解版本约束
用 pip list 与 import mmdet3d 验证安装是否成功
lectures.practice_task: 克隆仓库并从源码 pip install -e . ，打印 mmdet3d.__version__，并故意观察缺少 mmcv 时的报错信息，理解版本断言的作用。
lectures.title: 环境安装与版本验证

learning_goals: 使用 init_model 与 inference_detector 对单帧点云做检测
说出推理输入（点云文件）与输出（Det3DDataSample 中的 pred_instances_3d）的大致结构
对比 LidarDet3DInferencer 命令行方式与 API 方式的差异
lectures.practice_task: 下载 PointPillars KITTI 预训练权重，用 demo/pcd_demo.py 对 demo/data 目录中的点云跑通推理，并把检测结果保存为可视化图片。
lectures.title: 跑通第一个推理 Demo

learning_goals: 画出 mmdet3d 包内 datasets/structures/models/engine/evaluation/visualization 的依赖关系
说出 tools 目录下 train/test/create_data/analysis 各脚本的用途
明白 configs/_base_ 与 configs/<算法名>/ 的组织规律
lectures.practice_task: 手工绘制一张仓库模块依赖图：数据从 datasets 流向 structures 再流向 models，标注每个目录负责的职责，并指出 VoxelNet 类检测器涉及哪些子目录。
lectures.title: 仓库目录结构与源码地图

learning_goals: 读懂 _base_ 中 models/datasets/schedules/runtime 四类配置的职责
使用 --cfg-options 在命令行覆盖配置项
追踪一个完整配置最终会实例化哪些注册模块
lectures.practice_task: 用 tools/misc/print_config.py 展开 PointPillars KITTI 配置，找到 model、train_dataloader、val_evaluator 三大块，并修改 work_dir 与 batch_size 后重新展开对比差异。

units.title: 初识 MMDetection3D

learning_goals: 说出 LIDAR/CAM/DEPTH 三个坐标系的方向约定与适用场景
使用 Box3DMode 与 Coord3DMode 完成框和点的坐标系转换
理解转换矩阵（如 lidar2cam、Rt）在数据集中的存放位置
lectures.practice_task: 构造一个 LidarInstance3DBoxes，分别用 Box3DMode.convert 与 Coord3DMode.convert 把它转换到相机坐标系和深度坐标系，打印每次转换后的 tensor，验证 yaw 的符号翻转。
lectures.title: 三大坐标系与 Box3DMode/Coord3DMode

learning_goals: 解释 7 个自由度 tensor 的物理含义
使用 tensor 属性、bev、corners、nearest_be 方法
理解 LiDAR/Camera/Depth 三个子类的 yaw 约定差异
lectures.practice_task: 创建一个包含 3 个框的 DepthInstance3DBoxes，调用 in_range_bev 与 rotate，打印 bev 视图下的 2D 框坐标，并用 corners 验证旋转前后顶点位置是否符合右手系预期。
lectures.title: BaseInstance3DBoxes：7 自由度 3D 框的抽象

learning_goals: 理解 points_catdim 与张量布局 (N, point_dim)
使用 LiDARPoints 的 scale/rotate/flip/shift 方法
理解 LiDARPoints/CameraPoints/DepthPoints 之间的 convert 与 new_box 的配套关系
lectures.practice_task: 用 numpy 点云构造 LiDARPoints，依次执行 shift、rotate、flip，打印每步后的前 5 个点坐标；再用 convert_by_coord_type 把点转到相机坐标系并与手工矩阵乘法结果对比。
lectures.title: 点云结构：BasePoints 与三个坐标系子类

learning_goals: 区分 gt_instances_3d / pred_instances_3d / gt_pts_seg 等字段
理解 data_samples 如何在 DataLoader、模型、Evaluator 之间流转
会用 set_data / get 方法读写 DataSample
lectures.practice_task: 在 Python 中手工构造一个 Det3DDataSample，塞入一组 gt_instances_3d（3D 框 + labels_3d）和一组假的 pred_instances_3d，打印序列化结果，理解它在训练循环中承担的角色。
lectures.title: Det3DDataSample：贯穿训练推理的数据契约

units.title: 核心数据结构与坐标系统

learning_goals: 理解 MODALITIES、METAINFO 与 ann_file 的约定
追踪 load_data_list、get_data_info 与 parse_data_info 的调用链
理解 pipeline 在 dataset 初始化时是如何被 TRANSFORMS build 出来的
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 parse_data_info 在子类中的实现差异，写一段伪代码描述『一条 info 字典 → 一条训练样本 data_dict』的完整字段变化过程。
lectures.title: Det3DDataset 基类剖析

learning_goals: 使用 tools/create_data.py 为 KITTI/nuScenes 生成 info pkl
理解 kitti_converter 与 nuscenes_converter 各自产出的标注字段
理解 data/ 目录下的符号链接组织方式
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 create_data.py 的 dataset_converters 映射，写一个只含 2 帧的迷你 KITTI info pkl 生成调用命令（数据可缩放），并用 pandas/pickle 读出 pkl 打印一条 ann 记录的全部键。
lectures.title: 数据准备：从原始数据集到 info pkl

learning_goals: 比较 KITTI/nuScenes/Waymo/Lyft 的 parse_data_info 差异
理解 nuScenes 的 sweep 聚合与 lidar2cam 处理
理解 evaluate 如何与 metric 类配合
lectures.practice_task: 对比 nuscenes_dataset.py 与 kitti_dataset.py 的 parse_data_info 输出字典，列出相同字段与不同字段，并解释 sweeps/points 两个字段在管线中分别被哪个 Load 类消费。
lectures.title: 室外数据集：KITTI、nuScenes、Waymo、Lyft

learning_goals: 理解 ScanNet 与 SUN RGB-D 的 parse_data_info 输出结构
理解 Depth 坐标系在室内数据中的使用
理解 instance mask 与语义标签在 indoor 检测中的作用
lectures.practice_task: 用 tools/misc/browse_dataset.py 浏览 ScanNet 数据集（可使用 tiny 数据），观察一条样本经过 pipeline 前后的字段差异，记录 DepthInstance3DBoxes 的生成位置。

learning_goals: 说出 load_dim 与 use_dim 的语义

理解 mono3d 场景下图像与标定向量的加载方式

lectures.title: 数据加载 Transforms：LoadPointsFromFile 一族

learning_goals: 追踪 pcd_trans 与 box3d_centers 同步变换的实现
理解 GlobalRotScaleTrans 的旋转/缩放/平移参数如何同时作用于点和框

lectures.practice_task: 写一个 20 行的调试脚本，直接实例化 GlobalRotScaleTrans 并对一个随机场景（点 + 框）调用 transform，验证框中心与点云刚体变换的一致性。
lectures.title: 3D 数据增强：RandomFlip3D 与 GlobalRotScaleTrans

learning_goals: 理解 dbinfos pkl 的生成方式与组织结构
理解 BatchSampler 的按类采样与 DataBaseSampler.sample_all 流程

lectures.practice_task: 阅读 ObjectSample.transform，画出采样一个 Car 目标时『选样本→拼接点→平移框→修正 anchors』的流程图，并说明 min_points 过滤条件在哪里生效。
lectures.title: GT 数据库采样：ObjectSample 与 DataBaseSampler

learning_goals: 解释 keys_meta、gt_label_encode、filter_empty_gt 参数
区分训练阶段与推理阶段分别打包哪些字段
理解 data['inputs'] 与 data['data_samples'] 的最终形态
lectures.practice_task: 对一条经过完整增强管线的样本调用 Pack3DDetInputs，打印 data.keys() 与 data_samples 中所有 InstanceData 字段，梳理每个字段的消费者（模型/损失/评估）。
lectures.title: Pack3DDetInputs：数据管线的出口

units.title: 数据集与数据管线

learning_goals: 理解 parent registry 与 locations 自动导入机制
解释 config 中的 type='PointPillars' 如何路由到真实类
区分 MODELS/TRANSFORMS/DATASETS/METRICS 等注册节点
lectures.practice_task: 写一个最小示例：定义一个新的 BaseTransform 子类并用 TRANSFORMS.register_module() 注册，然后仅凭字典 dict(type='...') 从配置构建它，验证注册器查找链路。
lectures.title: 注册器机制：17 个注册节点如何串起全库

learning_goals: 解释 loss/predict/_forward 三种模式的数据流
理解 data_preprocessor 在 forward 之前如何接收 batch dict
对比 SingleStage3DDetector 与 MVXTwoStageDetector 的复用层次
lectures.practice_task: 绘制 Base3DDetector/SingleStage3DDetector/VoxelNet/TwoStage3DDetector 继承图，并在 SingleStage3DDetector.loss 中打点（本地实验）观察 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 的键。
lectures.title: 检测器分层体系：Base3DDetector 到具体检测器

learning_goals: 解释 batch_input_dim / pad_dims / max_num_points 等配置
理解 voxel_rescale_factor 在多尺度训练中的用途
追踪 forward 中 inputs dict 的 points key 如何变成 voxels
lectures.practice_task: 手工调用 VoxelizationByGridShape 或 VoxelGenerator（用伪点云 + 0.16m 柱体尺寸），打印 coors、voxels 形状与 num_points 分布，理解 batch 维度如何编进 coors。
lectures.title: Det3DDataPreprocessor 与体素化预处理

units.title: 模型体系与检测器基类

learning_goals: 按顺序说出 PillarFeatureEncoder、PillarScatter、backbone、neck、dense_head 的衔接
理解 PointPillars 无 z 维柱体的设计动机
对照 config 把每个模块的 type 与源码类一一对上
lectures.practice_task: 对照 configs/_base_/models/pointpillars_hv_secfpn_kitti.py，从下往上列出每层输入输出张量形状（柱体数、伪图像尺寸、通道数），并画出行数据流图。
lectures.title: VoxelNet 主流程与 PointPillars 全链路

learning_goals: 理解 sparse convolution 的 tensor 格式与 shape 转换
对比 SECOND backbone（2D 化后）与 SparseEncoder（全稀疏 UNet）的结构差异
理解稀疏卷积库（spconv/torchsparse/minkowski）的适配层
lectures.practice_task: 构造一个随机稀疏张量（indices + features），分别送入 SparseEncoder 的下采样段，打印每层输出通道与 indices 数量变化，理解稀疏 UNet 的跳跃连接。
lectures.title: SECOND Backbone 与稀疏编码器

learning_goals: 理解 SecFPN 与 FPN 在上/下采样方向的差别
追踪 neck 输出多尺度特征如何被 dense head 消费
理解 norm_cfg 与 act_cfg 的配置方法
lectures.practice_task: 修改 second_fpn 的 out_channels 并实例化，用伪多尺度特征（128/256/512 通道各一层）跑 forward，打印输出张量列表形状。
lectures.title: SECONDFPN：从 3D 特征到多尺度 BEV 特征

learning_goals: 理解 anchor3d 生成器的尺寸/旋转参数
理解 Anchor3DHead 多任务分支（热图/回归/方向/高度）的输出含义
理解 losses_by_num_level_sin_difference 中的 sin 差回归技巧
lectures.practice_task: 实例化 Anchor3DHead（参照 SECOND 配置的 num_classes/anchor size），用伪特征 forward，打印各分支输出张量形状与 anchor 数量，并核对 feature_map_size 与 anchor 总数的关系。
lectures.title: Anchor3DHead 与 3D 锚框生成

learning_goals: 理解 center heatmap 与 sub-heatmap 的分支含义
理解 CenterPointBBoxCoder 的编码/解码过程
对比 CenterPoint 与 SECOND 在 head 与 NMS 上的差异（含 CircleNMS）
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 CenterHead.get_targets，画出从 gt 3D 框生成 center heatmap 与 sub-center heatmap 的编码过程，并解释推理时 topK + peak extraction 的两阶段后处理顺序。
lectures.title: CenterPoint：Anchor-free 的中心点范式

learning_goals: 理解部分 bin-based 编码（AngleCoder 思想）的动机
理解 Max3DIoUAssigner 的正负样本分配准则与 match_low_quality 语义
理解 assign_result 与 sampling_result 的字段含义
lectures.practice_task: 用随机 anchors 和 gt 框直接调用 Max3DIoUAssigner.assign，打印 assigned_gt_inds 分布；再用 PartialBinBasedBBoxCoder 对一帧 gt 框做 encode→decode，统计解码误差。
lectures.title: 任务模块：BBox Coder、3D Assigner 与 Sampler

learning_goals: 理解 rotated IoU 的 box_converter 与 permute 实现
理解 MultibinLoss 的角度离散化与最优 bin 选择
区分 aligned 与普通 rotated NMS，以及 circle NMS 的适用场景
lectures.practice_task: 对两组已知交叠关系的 3D 框调用 RotatedIoULoss 与 multibin_loss，打印损失值，再分别用 rotated_nms_3d 与 aligned_rotated_nms_3d 做去重，比较保留框差异。
lectures.title: 3D 损失函数与 NMS

units.title: 基于体素/柱体的室外检测主线

理解 SSG 与 MSG 的差异
理解 stack 版本模块与 BasePointNet 的接口约定
lectures.practice_task: 用随机点云（N=16384, 3 通道）跑通 PointNet2SASSG.forward，打印每层 SA 模块输出点数与通道数，画出层级下采样表。
lectures.title: PointNet++ 系列骨干网络

learning_goals: 理解 object coordinate 与 center coordinate 的差别

追踪 get_bboxes 中 point2heatmap → aggregated points → proposal 的顺序

lectures.title: VoteNet：基于投票的室内检测端到端解析

理解 H3DNet 的 primitive（面/边/角）回归思想

lectures.title: 更多点云检测器：GroupFree3D、3DSSD、H3DNet

learning_goals: 理解 part 分支与 RoI 分支的耦合方式
理解 point2voxel 与 voxel RoI 特征提取的实现
理解 pv_rcnn_roi_head 的关键点采样分支

lectures.title: 两阶段检测器与 RoI Heads：Part-A2 与 PV-RCNN

理解 SMOKE 的 3D 中心点投影与尺寸回归

call_0906fb87b6fb4d3fb1289593.rationale: MMDetection3D 是基于 MMEngine 配置驱动架构的大型 3D 检测工具箱，代码量大、模块多，因此按「先会用、再懂结构、后懂算法、终能扩展」的顺序分 8 个单元 43 篇讲义。单元 1 让读者从零安装并跑通 demo，理解配置系统这一贯穿全库的骨架；单元 2 集中讲解坐标系与 BaseInstance3DBoxes/BasePoints/Det3DDataSample 这组全库通用的数据契约，这是 3D 领域最独特也最容易踩坑的部分，必须先于数据管线和模型讲解；单元 3 沿「原始数据 → info pkl → 数据集类 → 加载/增强/采样/打包管线」的真实数据流推进；单元 4 讲注册器机制与检测器基类，作为进入模型世界的门；单元 5、6 分别沿自动驾驶主线（体素/柱体 → SECOND → Anchor/CenterPoint → 任务模块与损失）和点云/单目/多模态主线（PointNet++ → VoteNet → 两阶段 → MVXNet）拆解模型算法，体素线在前因为它概念更少、链路最完整；单元 7 覆盖训练测试全流程、评估指标、可视化、推理器与实用工具；单元 8 面向二次开发，讲 3D 分割、自定义数据集与模型、projects 生态与测试贡献流程。依赖关系严格按数据结构 → 管线 → 模型 → 训练评估 → 扩展排列，确保每篇讲义只依赖已讲内容。

units.title: 3D 分割、扩展开发与项目生态

input.head: fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b
input.rationale: MMDetection3D 是基于 MMEngine 配置驱动架构的大型 3D 检测工具箱，代码量大、模块多，因此按「先会用、再懂结构、后懂算法、终能扩展」的顺序分 8 个单元 43 篇讲义。单元 1 让读者从零安装并跑通 demo，理解配置系统这一贯穿全库的骨架；单元 2 集中讲解坐标系与 BaseInstance3DBoxes/BasePoints/Det3DDataSample 这组全库通用的数据契约，这是 3D 领域最独特也最容易踩坑的部分，必须先于数据管线和模型讲解；单元 3 沿「原始数据 → info pkl → 数据集类 → 加载/增强/采样/打包管线」的真实数据流推进；单元 4 讲注册器机制与检测器基类，作为进入模型世界的门；单元 5、6 分别沿自动驾驶主线（体素/柱体 → SECOND → Anchor/CenterPoint → 任务模块与损失）和点云/单目/多模态主线（PointNet++ → VoteNet → 两阶段 → MVXNet）拆解模型算法，体素线在前因为它概念更少、链路最完整；单元 7 覆盖训练测试全流程、评估指标、可视化、推理器与实用工具；单元 8 面向二次开发，讲 3D 分割、自定义数据集与模型、projects 生态与测试贡献流程。依赖关系严格按数据结构 → 管线 → 模型 → 训练评估 → 扩展排列，确保每篇讲义只依赖已讲内容。

learning_goals: 说出 LIDAR/CAM/DEPTH 三个坐标系的方向约定与适用场景
使用 Box3DMode 与 Coord3DMode 完成框和点的坐标系转换
理解转换矩阵（如 lidar2cam、Rt）在数据集中的存放位置
lectures.practice_task: 构造一个 LidarInstance3DBoxes，分别用 Box3DMode.convert 与 Coord3DMode.convert 把它转换到相机坐标系和深度坐标系，打印每次转换后的 tensor，验证 yaw 的符号翻转。
lectures.title: 三大坐标系与 Box3DMode/Coord3DMode
lectures.topic: 讲清 LiDAR、相机、深度三个坐标系的方向约定，以及 Box3DMode 和 Coord3DMode 提供的框/点坐标系转换工具。

learning_goals: 解释 7 个自由度 tensor 的物理含义
使用 tensor 属性、bev、corners、nearest_be 方法
理解 LiDAR/Camera/Depth 三个子类的 yaw 约定差异
lectures.practice_task: 创建一个包含 3 个框的 DepthInstance3DBoxes，调用 in_range_bev 与 rotate，打印 bev 视图下的 2D 框坐标，并用 corners 验证旋转前后顶点位置是否符合右手系预期。
lectures.title: BaseInstance3DBoxes：7 自由度 3D 框的抽象
lectures.topic: 剖析 BaseInstance3DBoxes 及其三个坐标系子类，理解 3D 框张量表示、旋转、BEV 投影、corners 等核心方法。

learning_goals: 理解 points_catdim 与张量布局 (N, point_dim)
使用 LiDARPoints 的 scale/rotate/flip/shift 方法
理解 LiDARPoints/CameraPoints/DepthPoints 之间的 convert 与 new_box 的配套关系
lectures.practice_task: 用 numpy 点云构造 LiDARPoints，依次执行 shift、rotate、flip，打印每步后的前 5 个点坐标；再用 convert 把点转到相机坐标系并与手工矩阵乘法结果对比。
lectures.title: 点云结构：BasePoints 与三个坐标系子类
lectures.topic: 剖析 BasePoints/LiDARPoints/CameraPoints/DepthPoints，理解点云张量的存储布局与刚体变换方法。

learning_goals: 区分 gt_instances_3d / pred_instances_3d / gt_pts_seg 等字段
理解 data_samples 如何在 DataLoader、模型、Evaluator 之间流转
会用 set_data / get 方法读写 DataSample
lectures.practice_task: 在 Python 中手工构造一个 Det3DDataSample，塞入一组 gt_instances_3d（3D 框 + labels_3d）和一组假的 pred_instances_3d，打印序列化结果，理解它在训练循环中承担的角色。
lectures.title: Det3DDataSample：贯穿训练推理的数据契约
lectures.topic: 讲解 Det3DDataSample 与 PointData 两大数据容器，它们是数据管线输出、模型输入和评估输入的统一契约。

units.title: 核心数据结构与坐标系统

learning_goals: 理解 MODALITIES、METAINFO 与 ann_file 的约定
追踪 load_data_list、get_data_info 与 parse_data_info 的调用链
理解 pipeline 在 dataset 初始化时是如何被 TRANSFORMS build 出来的
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 parse_data_info 在子类中的实现差异，写一段伪代码描述『一条 info 字典 → 一条训练样本 data_dict』的完整字段变化过程。
lectures.title: Det3DDataset 基类剖析
lectures.topic: 讲解 Det3DDataset 如何继承 MMEngine 的 BaseDataset，负责 info 读取、metainfo 约定与数据管线构建。

learning_goals: 使用 tools/create_data.py 为 KITTI/nuScenes 生成 info pkl
理解 kitti_converter 与 nuscenes_converter 各自产出的标注字段
理解 data/ 目录下的符号链接组织方式
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 create_data.py 的 dataset_converters 映射，写出为 KITTI 生成 info pkl 的完整命令（数据可缩放），并用 pickle 读出 pkl 打印一条 ann 记录的全部键。
lectures.title: 数据准备：从原始数据集到 info pkl
lectures.topic: 讲解 tools/create_data.py 与各 dataset converter 如何把 KITTI/nuScenes/ScanNet 等原始数据转成统一 info pkl 和 GT 数据库。

learning_goals: 比较 KITTI/nuScenes/Waymo/Lyft 的 parse_data_info 差异
理解 nuScenes 的 sweep 聚合与 lidar2cam 处理
理解 evaluate 如何与 metric 类配合
lectures.practice_task: 对比 nuscenes_dataset.py 与 kitti_dataset.py 的 parse_data_info 输出字典，列出相同字段与不同字段，并解释 sweeps/points 两个字段在管线中分别被哪个 Load 类消费。
lectures.title: 室外数据集：KITTI、nuScenes、Waymo、Lyft
lectures.topic: 对比四个室外自动驾驶数据集类的实现差异，重点是 parse_data_info、坐标系选择与评估接口。

learning_goals: 理解 ScanNet 与 SUN RGB-D 的 parse_data_info 输出结构
理解 Depth 坐标系在室内数据中的使用
理解 instance mask 与语义标签在 indoor 检测中的作用
lectures.practice_task: 用 tools/misc/browse_dataset.py 浏览 ScanNet 数据集（可使用 tiny 数据），观察一条样本经过 pipeline 前后的字段差异，记录 DepthInstance3DBoxes 的生成位置。
lectures.title: 室内数据集：ScanNet 与 SUN RGB-D
lectures.topic: 讲解室内点云数据集类的实现，重点是深度坐标系、instance 分割标注与 VoteNet 类算法所需的数据格式。

learning_goals: 说出 load_dim 与 use_dim 的语义
理解 LoadPointsFromMultiSweeps 如何拼接多帧点云
理解 mono3d 场景下图像与标定向量的加载方式
lectures.practice_task: 对同一路 pipeline 分别设置 use_dim=[0,1,2] 与 use_dim=[0,1,2,3]，打印两种配置下进入 Pack3DDetInputs 的 points 张量形状，解释强度通道的影响。
lectures.title: 数据加载 Transforms：LoadPointsFromFile 一族
lectures.topic: 讲解 loading.py 中的 LoadPointsFromFile、LoadPointsFromMultiSweeps、LoadMultiViewImageFromFiles、LoadAnnotations3D 等加载类。

learning_goals: 追踪点云与 3D 框同步变换的实现
理解 GlobalRotScaleTrans 的旋转/缩放/平移参数如何同时作用于点和框
理解 ObjectRangeFilter / PointsRangeFilter 在增强末尾的作用
lectures.practice_task: 写一个 20 行的调试脚本，直接实例化 GlobalRotScaleTrans 并对一个随机场景（点 + 框）调用 transform，验证框中心与点云刚体变换的一致性。
lectures.title: 3D 数据增强：RandomFlip3D 与 GlobalRotScaleTrans
lectures.topic: 讲解 transforms_3d.py 中的几何与点级增强，重点是如何保证点云、3D 框与 2D 图像标注同步变换。

learning_goals: 理解 dbinfos pkl 的生成方式与组织结构
理解 BatchSampler 的按类采样与 DataBaseSampler.sample_all 流程
理解增强后 anchors 与 gt 的对应关系如何被修复
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 ObjectSample.transform，画出采样一个 Car 目标时『选样本→拼接点→平移框→修正 anchors』的流程图，并说明 min_points 过滤条件在哪里生效。
lectures.title: GT 数据库采样：ObjectSample 与 DataBaseSampler
lectures.topic: 讲解 GT-Amp 机制：create_gt_database 生成 dbinfos，DataBaseSampler 按类采样目标点云并粘贴到当前场景。

learning_goals: 解释 keys、meta_keys 等 dict 键的收集规则
区分训练与推理阶段分别打包哪些字段
理解 data['inputs'] 与 data['data_samples'] 的最终形态
lectures.practice_task: 对一条经过完整增强管线的样本调用 Pack3DDetInputs，打印 data.keys() 与 data_samples 中所有字段，梳理每个字段的消费者（模型/损失/评估）。
lectures.title: Pack3DDetInputs：数据管线的出口
lectures.topic: 讲解管线最后一个 transform Pack3DDetInputs 如何把 data dict 打包成 Det3DDataSample 与模型输入。

units.title: 数据集与数据管线

learning_goals: 理解 parent registry 与 locations 自动导入机制
解释 config 中的 type='PointPillars' 如何路由到真实类
区分 MODELS/TRANSFORMS/DATASETS/METRICS 等注册节点
lectures.practice_task: 写一个最小示例：定义一个新的 BaseTransform 子类并用 TRANSFORMS.register_module() 注册，然后仅凭字典 dict(type='...') 从配置构建它，验证注册器查找链路。
lectures.title: 注册器机制：17 个注册节点如何串起全库
lectures.topic: 讲解 mmdet3d/registry.py 中各注册节点的继承关系与 locations 自动导入机制，理解配置到类的路由。

learning_goals: 解释 loss/predict/_forward 三种模式的数据流
理解 data_preprocessor 在 forward 之前如何接收 batch dict
对比 SingleStage3DDetector 与 MVXTwoStageDetector 的复用层次
lectures.practice_task: 绘制 Base3DDetector/SingleStage3DDetector/VoxelNet/TwoStage3DDetector 继承图，并在 SingleStage3DDetector.loss 中打点（本地实验）观察 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 的键。
lectures.title: 检测器分层体系：Base3DDetector 到具体检测器
lectures.topic: 梳理 20 多个检测器类的继承树：Base3DDetector、SingleStage3DDetector、TwoStage3DDetector、MVXTwoStageDetector 等各自的角色。

learning_goals: 解释 voxel_size、max_num_points、grid_shape 等配置
理解 coors 中 batch 维的编码方式
追踪 forward 中 inputs dict 的 points 键如何变成 voxels
lectures.practice_task: 手工调用 VoxelGenerator（用伪点云 + 0.16m 柱体尺寸），打印 coors、voxels 形状与 num_points 分布，理解 batch 维度如何编进 coors。
lectures.title: Det3DDataPreprocessor 与体素化预处理
lectures.topic: 讲解 batch 归一化、堆叠以及 VoxelGenerator/VoxelizationByGridShape 等体素化前处理。

units.title: 模型体系与检测器基类

learning_goals: 按顺序说出 PillarFeatureEncoder、PillarScatter、backbone、neck、dense_head 的衔接
理解 PointPillars 无 z 维柱体的设计动机
对照 config 把每个模块的 type 与源码类一一对上
lectures.practice_task: 对照 configs/_base_/models/pointpillars_hv_secfpn_kitti.py，从下往上列出每层输入输出张量形状（柱体数、伪图像尺寸、通道数），并画出数据流图。
lectures.title: VoxelNet 主流程与 PointPillars 全链路
lectures.topic: 以 PointPillars 为例走通体素类检测器的完整前向：柱体编码 → 伪图像 scatter → 2D backbone → head。

learning_goals: 理解稀疏卷积的 indices/features 表示与 shape 转换
对比 SECOND backbone（2D 化后）与 SparseEncoder（全稀疏 UNet）的结构差异
理解 SubMConv3d 与 SparseConv3d 的区别
lectures.practice_task: 构造一个随机稀疏张量（indices + features），送入 SparseEncoder 的下采样段，打印每层输出通道与 indices 数量变化，理解稀疏 UNet 的跳跃连接。
lectures.title: SECOND Backbone 与稀疏编码器
lectures.topic: 讲解 SECOND 的 3D 稀疏卷积骨干与 SparseEncoder/SparseUNet 的稀疏 UNet 结构，理解稀疏卷积的组织方式。

learning_goals: 理解 SecFPN 与普通 FPN 在上/下采样方向的差别
追踪 neck 输出多尺度特征如何被 dense head 消费
理解 norm_cfg 与 act_cfg 的配置方法
lectures.practice_task: 修改 second_fpn 的 out_channels 并实例化，用伪多尺度特征（128/256/512 通道各一层）跑 forward，打印输出张量列表形状。
lectures.title: SECONDFPN：从 3D 特征到多尺度 BEV 特征
lectures.topic: 讲解 SECONDFPN 如何把稀疏骨干输出组合成多尺度 BEV 特征金字塔，以及 SecFPN 变体的含义。

learning_goals: 理解 anchor3d 生成器的尺寸/旋转参数
理解 Anchor3DHead 多任务分支（热图/回归/方向/高度）的输出含义
理解方向分类分支与 sin 差回归技巧的动机
lectures.practice_task: 实例化 Anchor3DHead（参照 SECOND 配置的 num_classes/anchor size），用伪特征 forward，打印各分支输出张量形状与 anchor 数量，并核对 feature_map_size 与 anchor 总数的关系。
lectures.title: Anchor3DHead 与 3D 锚框生成
lectures.topic: 讲解 Anchor3DHead 的多分支结构与 Anchor3DRangeGenerator 的 3D 锚框生成逻辑。

learning_goals: 理解 center heatmap 与子分支热图的含义
理解 CenterPointBBoxCoder 的编码/解码过程
对比 CenterPoint 与 SECOND 在 head 与 NMS 上的差异（含 CircleNMS）
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 CenterHead.get_targets，画出从 gt 3D 框生成 center heatmap 与 sub-heatmap 的编码过程，并解释推理时 topK 峰值提取的后处理顺序。
lectures.title: CenterPoint：Anchor-free 的中心点范式
lectures.topic: 讲解 CenterPoint 检测器与 CenterHead 的 center heatmap 分支设计，对比 anchor-based 范式。

learning_goals: 理解部分 bin-based 编码的动机与实现
理解 Max3DIoUAssigner 的正负样本分配准则
理解 assign_result 与 sampling_result 的字段含义
lectures.practice_task: 用随机 anchors 和 gt 框直接调用 Max3DIoUAssigner.assign，打印 assigned_gt_inds 分布；再用 PartialBinBasedBBoxCoder 对一帧 gt 框做 encode→decode，统计解码误差。
lectures.title: 任务模块：BBox Coder、3D Assigner 与 Sampler
lectures.topic: 讲解 task_modules 目录：各种 bbox coder 的编码方案、Max3DIoUAssigner 正负样本分配与采样器。

learning_goals: 理解 rotated IoU 的 box_converter 与 permute 实现
理解 MultibinLoss 的角度离散化与最优 bin 选择
区分 aligned 与普通 rotated NMS，以及 circle NMS 的适用场景
lectures.practice_task: 对两组已知交叠关系的 3D 框调用 RotatedIoULoss 与 multibin_loss，打印损失值，再分别用 rotated_nms_3d 与 aligned_rotated_nms_3d 做去重，比较保留框差异。
lectures.title: 3D 损失函数与 NMS
lectures.topic: 讲解 rotated IoU 损失、轴对齐 IoU 损失、Multibin 角度损失，以及 box3d_nms 中多种 NMS 变体。

units.title: 基于体素/柱体的室外检测主线

learning_goals: 理解 SA 模块的采样、分组、特征聚合三步骤
理解 SSG 与 MSG 的差异
理解 stack 版本模块与 BasePointNet 的接口约定
lectures.practice_task: 用随机点云（N=16384, 3 通道）跑通 PointNet2SASSG.forward，打印每层 SA 模块输出点数与通道数，画出层级下采样表。
lectures.title: PointNet++ 系列骨干网络
lectures.topic: 讲解 base_pointnet、PointNet2SASSG/MSG 骨干与 SA/FP 模块的三步抽象：采样、分组、聚合。

learning_goals: 理解 object coordinate 与 center coordinate 的差别
解释 vote 分支的偏移回归与种子点拓扑
追踪 get_bboxes 中投票点分组到 proposal 的顺序
lectures.practice_task: 阅读 VoteHead.forward + get_targets，画出『seed 点 → vote 偏移 → 分组聚类 → bbox head 打分』的数据流图，并用 configs/_base_/models/votenet.py 核对每层通道数。
lectures.title: VoteNet：基于投票的室内检测端到端解析
lectures.topic: 端到端讲解 VoteNet：PointNet++ 骨干 → VoteModule 投票 → 分组 → VoteHead 出框。

learning_goals: 理解 transformer 解码器在 GroupFree3D 中的作用
理解 3DSSD 的辅助分支设计
理解 H3DNet 的 primitive（面/边/角）回归思想
lectures.practice_task: 对比三种 head 的 get_targets 实现，写一张对比表：候选点来源、分组方式、分类回归分支数、解码器类型，并用各自 config 验证。
lectures.title: 更多点云检测器：GroupFree3D、3DSSD、H3DNet
lectures.topic: 横向对比三个进阶室内点云检测器的候选点生成、注意力机制与几何基元回归。

learning_goals: 理解 part 分支与 RoI 分支的耦合方式
理解 point2voxel 与 voxel RoI 特征提取的实现
理解 pv_rcnn_roi_head 的关键点采样分支
lectures.practice_task: 画出 PartA2 与 PV-RCNN 的两阶段结构对比图（RPN→RoI 特征来源→bbox head），并指出它们的 RoI 特征提取器类名与差异。
lectures.title: 两阶段检测器与 RoI Heads：Part-A2 与 PV-RCNN
lectures.topic: 讲解 roi_heads 子系统的组织：base_3droi_head、roi_extractors、bbox_heads，以及 Part-A2/PV-RCNN 两个两阶段检测器。

learning_goals: 理解 SingleStageMono3DDetector 的复用结构
理解 FCOS3D head 的 bbox_coder（深度/朝向/尺寸）设计
理解 SMOKE 的 3D 中心点投影与尺寸回归
lectures.practice_task: 用 FCOS3D config 实例化 head，随机图像特征 forward，打印每个输出分支张量形状，并把 bbox_coder 的解码输出投影回图像平面验证 2D 框合理性。
lectures.title: 单目 3D 检测：FCOS3D、SMOKE 与相机坐标系
lectures.topic: 讲解单目 3D 检测分支：SingleStageMono3DDetector 及 FCOS3D/SMOKE 等 head 的相机坐标系设计。

learning_goals: 理解 MVXTwoStageDetector 如何复用 2D 检测组件
理解 MMDetection 组件在 3D 项目中的直接复用方式
理解图像特征如何映射回 voxel 做融合
lectures.practice_task: 对照 mvxnet config 列出其中哪些模块实际来自 mmdet（如 RoIHead/Backbone），画出『点云分支 + 图像分支』在 extract_feat 与 roi_head 阶段的汇合点。
lectures.title: 多模态融合检测：MVXNet 与 mmdet 组件复用
lectures.topic: 讲解 MVXTwoStageDetector 与 MVXFasterRCNN 如何同时吃点云和图像，并复用 MMDetection 的 2D 检测组件。

units.title: 点云原生检测器、单目与多模态

learning_goals: 说出 Runner 从 cfg 构建 runner 到启动 train loop 的步骤
理解 amp、sync_bn、resume、cfg-options 各参数的实现位置
理解 optim_wrapper/param_scheduler 的配置组织
lectures.practice_task: 用 KITTI PointPillars 配置做 1 个 epoch 的最小训练（可缩数据集），在 work_dir 中找到 log、checkpoint 与 vis_data，并解释 log 中 dataloader 与 iter 耗时字段。
lectures.title: train.py 与 Runner 训练全流程
lectures.topic: 从 tools/train.py 入手讲解配置解析、Runner 构建、AMP/SyncBN/resume 处理与训练主循环。

learning_goals: 理解 test.py 如何 build model/dataloader/evaluator
解释 NuScenesMetric 的 mAP、NDS、mATE 等指标计算过程
理解 KittiMetric 对 difficulty 与 2D/3D AP 的处理
lectures.practice_task: 对训练出的 PointPillars 模型运行 tools/test.py，对比不同 score_thr 阈值下的 mAP 变化，并阅读 compute_metrics 在 NuScenesMetric 中的调用点。
lectures.title: test.py 与评估指标体系
lectures.topic: 讲解测试入口与各数据集的 metric 实现：NuScenesMetric 的 NDS、KittiMetric 的 AP、WaymoMetric 与室内指标。

learning_goals: 理解 Visualizer 的多后端（local、tensorboard）适配
理解 Det3DLocalVisualizer 如何画 3D 框与多模态投影
理解 Vis3DHook 触发频率与保存路径配置
lectures.practice_task: 对推理结果调用 Det3DLocalVisualizer 的检测绘制接口，用 BEV 与点云投影两种方式各输出一张图，并解释 3D 框颜色与类别映射来源。
lectures.title: 可视化系统：Det3DLocalVisualizer 与 Hook
lectures.topic: 讲解 Det3DLocalVisualizer、Vis3DHook 与 vis_utils 如何在训练与推理阶段绘制 3D 框和点云投影。

learning_goals: 理解 inferencer 如何用 config 与 checkpoint 驱动推理
理解 MultiViewWrapper 与 merge_aug_bboxes_3d 的 TTA 逻辑
理解 pipeline 与 tta_pipeline 两套配置的关系
lectures.practice_task: 用 LidarDet3DInferencer（CLI 或 Python）对 demo 点云推理并保存结果，再参照 CenterPoint flip-tta 配置，说明多增强结果在 merge 阶段如何合并。
lectures.title: 高阶推理：Inferencer 体系与 TTA
lectures.topic: 讲解 4 类 Inferencer（LiDAR/单目/多模态检测与 LiDAR 分割）与 MultiViewWrapper + merge_augs 的测试时增强。

learning_goals: 会用 analyze_logs 画 loss/mAP 曲线

call_3d896c87054d41b381537239.head: fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b
call_3d896c87054d41b381537239.rationale: MMDetection3D 是基于 MMEngine 配置驱动架构的大型 3D 检测工具箱，代码量大、模块多，因此按「先会用、再懂结构、后懂算法、终能扩展」的顺序分 8 个单元 43 篇讲义。单元 1 让读者从零安装并跑通 demo，理解配置系统这一贯穿全库的骨架；单元 2 集中讲解坐标系与 BaseInstance3DBoxes/BasePoints/Det3DDataSample 这组全库通用的数据契约，这是 3D 领域最独特也最容易踩坑的部分，必须先于数据管线和模型讲解；单元 3 沿「原始数据 → info pkl → 数据集类 → 加载/增强/采样/打包管线」的真实数据流推进；单元 4 讲注册器机制与检测器基类，作为进入模型世界的门；单元 5、6 分别沿自动驾驶主线（体素/柱体 → SECOND → Anchor/CenterPoint → 任务模块与损失）和点云/单目/多模态主线（PointNet++ → VoteNet → 两阶段 → MVXNet）拆解模型算法，体素线在前因为它概念更少、链路最完整；单元 7 覆盖训练测试全流程、评估指标、可视化、推理器与实用工具；单元 8 面向二次开发，讲 3D 分割、自定义数据集与模型、projects 生态与测试贡献流程。依赖关系严格按数据结构 → 管线 → 模型 → 训练评估 → 扩展排列，确保每篇讲义只依赖已讲内容。

units.title: 3D 分割、扩展开发与项目生态

data.head: fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b
data.rationale: MMDetection3D 是基于 MMEngine 配置驱动架构的大型 3D 检测工具箱，代码量大、模块多，因此按「先会用、再懂结构、后懂算法、终能扩展」的顺序分 8 个单元 43 篇讲义。单元 1 让读者从零安装并跑通 demo，理解配置系统这一贯穿全库的骨架；单元 2 集中讲解坐标系与 BaseInstance3DBoxes/BasePoints/Det3DDataSample 这组全库通用的数据契约，这是 3D 领域最独特也最容易踩坑的部分，必须先于数据管线和模型讲解；单元 3 沿「原始数据 → info pkl → 数据集类 → 加载/增强/采样/打包管线」的真实数据流推进；单元 4 讲注册器机制与检测器基类，作为进入模型世界的门；单元 5、6 分别沿自动驾驶主线（体素/柱体 → SECOND → Anchor/CenterPoint → 任务模块与损失）和点云/单目/多模态主线（PointNet++ → VoteNet → 两阶段 → MVXNet）拆解模型算法，体素线在前因为它概念更少、链路最完整；单元 7 覆盖训练测试全流程、评估指标、可视化、推理器与实用工具；单元 8 面向二次开发，讲 3D 分割、自定义数据集与模型、projects 生态与测试贡献流程。依赖关系严格按数据结构 → 管线 → 模型 → 训练评估 → 扩展排列，确保每篇讲义只依赖已讲内容。
